fixed.title: 12 Holy Nights End (Epiphany)
fixed.desc: Epiphany closes the Twelve Holy Nights and opens the season of Epiphany: the light of Christmas carried out into the year.

img.alt: Adoration of the Magi, Gentile da Fabriano (1423)

fixed.title: Candlemas
fixed.desc: Forty days after Christmas: the midpoint between winter solstice and spring equinox, traditionally a festival of candles and returning light.

img.alt: Presentation of Christ in the Temple, Giotto, Scrovegni Chapel (c. 1305)

fixed.title: St. John's Tide (Johanni)
fixed.desc: Festival of John the Baptist near midsummer. Steiner described it as the time when the Earth breathes out most fully into the cosmos; often celebrated with a bonfire.

img.alt: St. John's fire (Johannisfeuer) burning at night

fixed.title: Michaelmas - Festival of Courage
fixed.desc: Festival of the Archangel Michael at the turn to autumn. Steiner hoped it would become a festival of courage and inner strength as nature dies back.

img.alt: St. Michael and the Dragon, Raphael (c. 1505)

fixed.title: Martinmas (Lantern Walk)
fixed.desc: Feast of St. Martin, who shared his cloak with a beggar. In Waldorf communities children carry lanterns: carrying an inner light into the darkening season.

img.alt: Glowing paper sun lantern for St. Martin's lantern walk

fixed.title: St. Nicholas Day
fixed.desc: Feast of St. Nicholas of Myra, patron of children; small gifts are left in shoes the night before.

img.alt: Icon of St. Nicholas of Myra (1294)

fixed.title: 12 Holy Nights Begin
fixed.desc: Christmas Eve. The Twelve Holy Nights begin: a time for inner quiet, review of the past year and preparing the year ahead. Traditions differ on whether the first night is that of 24 or 25 December.

img.alt: Rudolf Steiner's apocalyptic seal: the woman clothed with the sun, moon at her feet

fixed.title: Christmas - Birth of Light
fixed.desc: The festival of the birth of Christ and of the light reborn at the darkest time of the year.

img.alt: The Nativity, Giotto, Scrovegni Chapel (c. 1305)

easter.title: Ash Wednesday
easter.desc: Beginning of Lent, the forty days of preparation for Easter.

img.alt: Ash Wednesday (Aschermittwoch), Carl Spitzweg (c. 1860)

easter.title: Palm Sunday
easter.desc: Entry into Jerusalem; the beginning of Holy Week.

img.alt: Entry into Jerusalem, Giotto, Scrovegni Chapel (c. 1305)

easter.title: Maundy Thursday
easter.desc: The Last Supper and the washing of the feet.

img.alt: The Last Supper, Leonardo da Vinci (1495-1498)

easter.title: Good Friday
easter.desc: The Crucifixion. In the Parzival saga, the day the Grail is renewed.

img.alt: The Crucifixion, Isenheim Altarpiece, Matthias Grünewald (1512-1516)

easter.title: Holy Saturday
easter.desc: The day in the grave: the descent into the depths of the Earth.

img.alt: The Body of the Dead Christ in the Tomb, Hans Holbein the Younger (1521-1522)

easter.title: Easter - Festival of Resurrection
easter.desc: First Sunday after the first full moon after the spring equinox. Its date is set by sun and moon together, which Steiner discussed in his 1924 Easter lectures.

img.alt: The Resurrection, Isenheim Altarpiece, Matthias Grünewald (1512-1516)

easter.title: Ascension
easter.desc: Forty days after Easter: the Ascension of Christ.

img.alt: The Ascension, Giotto, Scrovegni Chapel (c. 1305)

easter.title: Pentecost (Whitsun) - Awakening of Spirit
easter.desc: Fifty days after Easter. Steiner called Whitsun the festival of the free individuality.

img.alt: Rudolf Steiner, apocalyptic seal 7: the dove above the Grail cup

easter.title: Trinity Sunday
easter.desc: The Sunday after Pentecost, closing the Easter season.

img.alt: The Holy Trinity icon, Andrei Rublev (c. 1411-1425)

anniversaries.title: First Waldorf School opened (Stuttgart)
anniversaries.desc: The Free Waldorf School on the Uhlandshoehe in Stuttgart opened for the children of Waldorf-Astoria factory workers, founded by Emil Molt with Rudolf Steiner.

img.alt: Freie Waldorfschule Uhlandshöhe, Stuttgart, the first Waldorf school

anniversaries.title: First Goetheanum destroyed by fire
anniversaries.desc: The First Goetheanum, the double-domed wooden headquarters of the Anthroposophical Society in Dornach, Switzerland, was destroyed by fire on New Year's Eve, 31 December 1922. It burned through the night into 1 January 1923.

img.alt: Smouldering ruins of the First Goetheanum after the fire, 1923

anniversaries.title: Christmas Conference opens (Dornach)
anniversaries.desc: The Christmas Conference (24 December 1923 to 1 January 1924) was the foundational gathering led by Rudolf Steiner in Dornach, Switzerland, to refound the General Anthroposophical Society. It met beside the ruins of the First Goetheanum, lost to fire a year earlier.

img.alt: Rudolf Steiner's blackboard drawing of the second Goetheanum motif, 1 January 1924 (Christmas Conference)

anniversaries.title: Foundation Stone laid (Christmas Conference)
anniversaries.desc: At the Christmas Conference in Dornach (24 December 1923 to 1 January 1924) Steiner refounded the General Anthroposophical Society and laid the Foundation Stone meditation on 25 December.

img.alt: Rudolf Steiner's blackboard drawing of the second Goetheanum motif, 1 January 1924 (Christmas Conference)

anniversaries.title: Agriculture Course begins (Koberwitz)
anniversaries.desc: Steiner gave the eight lectures of the Agriculture Course at Koberwitz, 7 to 16 June 1924: the beginning of biodynamic farming.

img.alt: Koberwitz manor (Kobierzyce palace), site of the 1924 Agriculture Course

anniversaries.title: Last Stand of the Cathars at Montsegur
anniversaries.desc: The Chateau de Montsegur, a mountain fortress in the French Pyrenees, surrendered after a nine-month siege. On 16 March 1244 about 210 Cathars were burned at the foot of the mountain.

anniversaries.title: Last Stand of the Knights Templar
anniversaries.desc: On 13 October 1307 King Philip IV of France orchestrated the simultaneous, surprise arrest of hundreds of Knights Templar across France. Pope Clement V dissolved the order at the Council of Vienne in 1312.

anniversaries.title: Fall of the Spirits of Darkness and Beginning of the Michael Age
anniversaries.desc: According to Rudolf Steiner's spiritual research, the Michael Age began in November 1879, after the Archangel Michael cast down the Spirits of Darkness.

memorials.name: Rudolf Steiner
memorials.desc: Rudolf Steiner died in Dornach, Switzerland, on 30 March 1925, at the age of 64, in his studio beside the building site of the second Goetheanum.

img.alt: Rudolf Steiner in Dornach, 1914
